title: A tiny grep
hints: Count lines as you scan, starting at 1. strings.Contains(line, pattern) decides whether a line matches.
bufio.Scanner's default line splitter already removes a \r before the \n, so Windows line endings come out clean. Splitting the text yourself on "\n" would leave the \r behind.
Write matches with fmt.Fprintf(w, "%d:%s\n", lineNo, line), count them, and return sc.Err() at the end.
